snippet.description:
Waves of Russian missile and drone attacks on Ukraine’s capital Kyiv have killed 23 people with almost 90 others injured.

The city’s mayor called the nighttime strikes “terrible” and declared Friday as a day of mourning.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Vladimir Putin was losing the war and would only escalate his attacks on civilians. 

In Moscow and St Petersburg citizens are now also feeling its impact: fuel shortages have created long lines that bristle with dissent. Usually loyal commentators are questioning the point of the war and Putin has admitted that there are problems while still vowing to escalate. 

The dead and injured have been pulled from rubble in the capital Kyiv. But does Putin feel for the first time that he might lose the war he started?

snippet.title: Your Attention Is Being Sold | Yasmine Bennis | TEDxDAA Youth
snippet.description: When was the last time you were truly alone with your own thoughts? Or completed a full task without checking social media? Or been able to sit down for a few minutes without being distracted? Our world monetizes distraction - your attention is worth more than you can imagine. But, how much does it cost you? In her talk, Yasmine will explore how technology - specifically addiction - can rewire your brain and your body, and how we can take that control back. Yasmine is a grade 8 student from Morocco and Canada who is interested in science, swimming, and reading. She is passionate about real-world issues that affect her generation. Yasmine has a deep interest in psychology & human behavior, using both personal experiences and research to understand phone addiction, attention, and the way technology shapes the modern world. She urges the audience to find their individual solution to phone addiction, bringing attention to the normalization of it. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

snippet.title: India's last nomads | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
This film tells the story of Ahmed and his family, camel herders in the deserts of western India. For generations, they’ve roamed the barren land with their animals, leading lives shaped by tradition and nature.

But this way of life is coming under increasing pressure: industrialization, climate change and economic challenges are rapidly transforming the region and threatening the future of nomadic life.
The film follows the family over an extended period, offering a rare insight into their daily lives. With great intimacy, it shows how they search for water sources, tend to their animals and travel through the desolate landscapes. In quiet conversations by the fire or whilst on the move, it becomes clear just how much Ahmed and his family are caught between the past and the future. They wrestle with the question of whether to continue along the old paths or to provide their children with a different, supposedly safer life.

The documentary relies on the simple power of observation. The calm, atmospheric images create an intimate connection with the protagonists, and underline what’s at stake: not just a way of life, but an understanding of how to live in harmony with nature. Relationships between people, animals and the landscape merge, in a delicate fabric - all part of a cultural heritage that may soon disappear.

The film is much more than a portrait; it exemplifies how traditional communities worldwide can be torn apart by the tensions of an accelerating present. At the same time, it invites the audience to appreciate the beauty and significance of a way of life that, despite all challenges, retains a remarkable dignity.

snippet.title: L'ultima generazione che può permettersi di sbagliare | Claudio Casisa | TEDxPoliteama
snippet.description: In un’epoca dominata dalla ricerca ossessiva della perfezione, della velocità e dall'influenza crescente dell'intelligenza artificiale, siamo costantemente spinti a confrontarci con standard irraggiungibili. Claudio Casisa, con la sua inconfondibile ironia, ci invita a fare un passo indietro, rivendicando il valore profondo e autentico delle nostre imperfezioni. Attraverso il racconto sincero e dissacrante dei suoi difetti, l’attore comico ci ricorda che il vero "supereroe" non è chi appare impeccabile, ma chi ha il coraggio di dichiararsi umano. Un invito prezioso a celebrare l'errore e il disagio come ultimi, irripetibili tratti distintivi della nostra civiltà, prima che la tecnologia ci guidi verso una perfezione priva di umanità. Claudio Casisa, comico e attore palermitano, classe '91. Nella stagione 2011-2012 partecipa insieme a “Le Malerbe” al programma televisivo Le Iene. Nel 2014 forma, insieme ad Annandrea Vitrano, il duo comico I Soldi Spicci. Il duo prende parte a diversi programmi televisivi tra cui Colorado Café e Pechino Express e realizza diverse tournée teatrali in giro per l’Italia: Femmino e maschia (2013), Chi dice donna dice camion (2019) e Tutta colpa del Poliamore (2023). Nell’autunno 2018 esce al cinema il loro primo film “La fuitina sbagliata”, distribuito da Rai Cinema e 01 Distribution. Nel settembre 2022 il duo debutta in regia con il secondo film “Un mondo Sotto Social”, prodotto da Tramp Ltd e distribuito da Medusa Film. Nel 2024 presenta il primo progetto teatrale da solista "Spaiato" e nel 2026 porta il suo nuovo monologo  di standup "Inconcludente". This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

snippet.title: De nouveaux récits pour un monde durable | Marketing & imaginaires | Thomas PAROUTY | TEDxSaclay
snippet.description:
Nos récits créent nos imaginaires et façonnent nos désirs.
Depuis la Grotte de Lascaux, l’homme se raconte des histoires, pour transmettre sa culture et se projeter dans le futur. La culture issue du cinéma, de la TV, des réseaux sociaux ou de la publicité a transformé nos cultures populaires, bourgeoises, syndicales… en une seule grande culture de la consommation.
Cette hyperproduction casse les limites planétaires. Il est donc urgent de réinventer nos récits.
Les marques devront nous proposer des récits de consommation joyeuse et d’usage partagé plutôt que de propriété égoïste. Elles doivent proposer un nouvel imaginaire de bonheur, pour casser les normes sociales actuelles et inventer un nouvel avenir sobre et désirable. Après trois années passées au Chili pour Pasteur, Thomas débute sa carrière dans de grandes agences de communication. En 2009, il fonde MIEUX, la première agence de communication dédiée à la RSE. Avec son équipe, il accompagne les entreprises dans la valorisation de leurs engagements auprès de leurs collaborateurs, clients et territoires, tout en contribuant au lancement de produits et services plus durables, locaux et circulaires. Entreprise à mission, MIEUX a été élue Agence Communication RSE de l’année. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

Salmon consumption has skyrocketed, making it one of the most popular fish across the US, Europe and Japan. To meet this huge demand, over 500 million salmon are farmed every year, accounting for around 70% of total global salmon supply. Norway dominates the industry as the world's leading producer.   

Up to 120,000 salmon are often confined within a single net-pen. Overcrowding provides ideal conditions for the rapid spread of diseases and parasites. In 2023 alone, more than 60 million farmed salmon died prematurely in Norway. The causes were severe disease outbreaks and fatal injuries suffered during aggressive treatments used to combat parasites. 

As the aquaculture industry expands, experts and activists are increasingly questioning the sustainability and ethics of these high-intensity farming methods.

snippet.title: Nessa Barrett & Her Loneliness 😔
snippet.description:
🎤 Welcome to Nessa Barrett's heartfelt interview on the Jay Shatty Podcast! 😢 In this candid conversation, Nessa opens up about her personal experience with loneliness, taking us on a journey through the highs and lows of her life as a rising star in the music industry. 🌟

Join us as Nessa delves into the raw emotions she faced after her exhilarating tour, giving us a glimpse into the real-life struggles that often go unnoticed behind the glamorous facade. 🏨 From the overwhelming feelings of isolation in a hotel room to the challenges of navigating the cutthroat Hollywood environment, Nessa sheds light on the often unspoken hardships that come with fame and success. 🎭

With remarkable honesty, she shares her quest to find genuine connections in a world where superficiality often prevails. Navigating the glitzy world of showbiz, Nessa gives us a glimpse of the hurdles she encountered while trying to find her tribe, emphasizing just how difficult it can be to find authentic and supportive people in such an intense and competitive industry. 🌈

This conversation is not only an eye-opener into the personal struggles of a young artist but also a reminder that everyone, regardless of fame or popularity, can experience loneliness and yearn for meaningful connections. Nessa's journey serves as an inspiration to those who may be facing their own battles with loneliness, reminding us all that vulnerability and authenticity are essential in finding genuine companionship and support. 💖

snippet.title: Canada's multicultural metropolis: When night falls in Toronto | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
"We're just like New York," they say of their city, and usually add: "Only nicer!" Toronto is a melting pot of diverse cultures. Most of its residents have immigrated, at some point.

The documentary features the Neon Riders of Toronto, decorating their bikes with colorful lights and heading out at night for a ride and a party. Then there’s 28-year-old Jill, who opts to spend the night catching raccoons instead of losing herself on a club dancefloor. Or Quinn, who upholds the traditions of his Indigenous ancestors through painted constellations. And the guys from the Latino band ‘6ix Pal Mundo’, who are creating a new soundtrack for the city.
These are just a few of the many stories and moments in a film about a city that welcomes everyone, is beautiful but never pretentious, and doesn’t beg to be loved -- but is adored by its inhabitants. A place where entering the world’s largest underground pedestrian tunnel system can feel like taking a journey through several different continents.

Canada’s largest city lives up to its promise of being a thriving multicultural metropolis. Seven million people from over 230 nations live in the Greater Toronto Area. As most residents will tell you with pride, if you make the most of your opportunities, you can achieve anything here. One of the reasons why Toronto is arguably the fastest-growing city in North America. But that brings another set of problems: the number of homeless people has doubled within four years, to more than 15,000.

snippet.title: New York Hustle | The Economy of Survival
snippet.description:
New York Hustle - In New York City, survival itself becomes a full-time job. From subway performers and Times Square hustlers to street artists and immigrant vendors, New York Hustle reveals the hidden economy powering one of the richest cities in the world. This documentary explores ambition, struggle, creativity and survival in a city where millions are forced to invent their own way to live. Because in modern cities… hustle is no longer a choice, it’s an economic necessity.

New York Hustle

Created By: Angelica Von Helle, Matt Reekie
Directors: Angelica Von Helle, Matt Reekie 
Writers: Angelica Von Helle, Matt Reekie
Stars: Astro Erle, Timmy the Traineater, Stuart Gray, Miguel, Lance.
Genre: Documentary, Society, Urban Life
Country: United States
Language: English
Filming Locations: New York City, USA

Synopsis:

New York Hustle is an episodic documentary series profiling street-level entrepreneurs operating across the boroughs of New York City. Each episode follows individuals who have created unconventional ways of making a living in one of the most competitive and expensive cities in the world.

From subway performers and street artists to informal vendors and Times Square characters, the series captures the creativity, resilience, and survival instincts that define New York’s hustle culture. Through intimate portraits and observational storytelling, the documentary explores the economic realities of urban life and the blurred line between entrepreneurship, performance, and survival.

The series also highlights the diversity of New York’s informal economy, showing how people transform public spaces, talent, and personality into income streams while navigating the pressures of life in a constantly changing city.

snippet.title: The Psychology Of People Who Don’t Post Their Photos
snippet.description:
The Psychology Of People Who Don’t Post Their Photos

Have you ever wondered why some people choose to live quietly online, scrolling, observing, but never posting a selfie? Most assume it's fear, shyness, or insecurity. But the truth is far more complex and fascinating.

This video dives deep into the layered psychology of individuals who choose invisibility over exposure. We explore how they operate from an 'internal locus of identity,' valuing presence over performance, and why they see privacy not as avoidance, but as a crucial form of emotional strength and self-respect.

If you've ever felt that strange discomfort before posting a picture, this story is for you. Discover why their choice is not about hiding from the world, but about experiencing it more deeply, protecting their essence from being reduced to a single image, and prioritizing authenticity over digital applause. Their silence speaks volumes. Watch to understand the wisdom of choosing not to be seen.

snippet.title: How Complaining Destroys Your Brain.
snippet.description:
How Complaining Destroys Your Brain. 

Most people think complaining is just something they do when they're frustrated. The brain sees it differently. Every repeated thought strengthens the neural pathways responsible for producing it. When criticism and complaints become a daily habit, the brain becomes more efficient at generating the same patterns again and again. Over time, this can shift attention toward what's wrong, what's missing, and what could go badly. The result is not necessarily that life becomes worse, but that the brain becomes faster at finding reasons to experience it that way. snippet.title: You Are Weak Because Of Your Father
snippet.description:
You Are Weak Because Of Your Father

There's a quiet truth many of us carry: the heaviness we feel—the self-doubt, the anxiety, the feeling of being perpetually weak or stuck—often didn't start with us. It's tied to the emotional environment, the unspoken rules, and the inner voice we inherited from the man who raised us.

This video is a deep dive into the concept of emotional inheritance. We explore how your father's fears, silence, anger, or absence shaped your nervous system, teaching you survival mechanisms (like avoidance or perfectionism) that now limit you in adulthood. You weren't weak; you were adapting. 

We discuss the critical difference between true strength and emotional conditioning, and how the blueprint for your relationship with yourself was established by your relationship with him. 

But here's the powerful realization: You don't have to continue the story you were handed. Healing begins with awareness. This video guides you toward understanding the origin of your patterns so you can finally rewrite your own future and build a definition of strength rooted in who you truly are. 

If you've ever struggled with indecision, guilt, people-pleasing, or the inability to rest, this message is for you.

snippet.title: The Psychology of the Child Who Was Always Compared
snippet.description:
The Psychology of the Child Who Was Always Compared

Some children don't grow up feeling unseen—they grow up feeling *measured*. If you were constantly compared to siblings, cousins, or an idealized version of yourself, this video is for you. We explore the profound, often hidden, ways that constant comparison shapes your adult life: from overworking out of fear, struggling to trust unconditional love, to battling existential exhaustion and self-sabotaging success. Comparison taught you how to perform, but it also taught your nervous system that connection is conditional. We dive into the psychology of perfectionism driven by fear, the loss of intrinsic motivation, and the subtle ways your body holds onto vigilance. Healing isn't about becoming more confident; it's about shifting from comparison to curiosity, embracing the grief for the child who never got to just be, and finding true alignment. Learn how to reclaim your internal time and finally exist without the need to be exceptional.

Some children don't grow up feeling unseen—they grow up feeling *measured*. If you were constantly compared to siblings, cousins, or an idealized version of yourself, this video is for you. We explore the profound, often hidden, ways that constant comparison shapes your adult life: from overworking out of fear, struggling to trust unconditional love, to battling existential exhaustion and self-sabotaging success. Comparison taught you how to perform, but it also taught your nervous system that connection is conditional. We dive into the psychology of perfectionism driven by fear, the loss of intrinsic motivation, and the subtle ways your body holds onto vigilance. Healing isn't about becoming more confident; it's about shifting from comparison to curiosity, embracing the grief for the child who never got to just be, and finding true alignment. Learn how to reclaim your internal time and finally exist without the need to be exceptional.

snippet.title: The Power of Being Alone.
snippet.description:
The Power of Being Alone. 

Most people think being alone is something to avoid. The moment there is silence, they reach for a phone, a conversation, or another distraction. But solitude has a way of revealing things that constant noise keeps hidden. When nobody is telling you who to be, what to believe, or what success should look like, you finally get the chance to hear your own thoughts clearly. That is where real self-awareness begins. Kevin Levrone understood that growth is not always built in front of an audience. Sometimes it is built in the quiet moments when nobody is watching. The more time you spend alone with your thoughts, the easier it becomes to separate your own voice from everyone else's expectations. What many people call loneliness can become one of the most powerful tools for clarity, purpose, and direction.

#solitude #clarity #innerpeace

snippet.title: Banned weapons - Why Europe is bringing back landmines | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
Landmines can maim and kill civilians and are banned in many countries under the 1997 Ottawa Treaty. Yet on Europe’s northeastern border, these controversial weapons are making a comeback.

Following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Finland, Poland, and the Baltic states are rearming and bringing banned anti-personnel landmines (APLs) back into their arsenals. While military and political leaders say they contribute to strategic deterrence, mine victims and deminers say they pose a serious long-term danger. 
The war in Ukraine has reshaped Europe’s security thinking and triggered a radical shift in Finland. According to Colonel Riku Mikkonen of the Finnish armed forces, the military considers APLs a cost effective tool for national defence and a pragmatic instrument of deterrence. 
But to Zoran Ješić, who lost a leg to a mine in the Bosnian war, these weapons continue to kill, maim and render entire regions uninhabitable even decades after conflicts have ended. His story illustrates the long-term consequences of weapons that are banned by more than 160 countries.
In Helsinki, Left Alliance politician Li Andersson opposes their reintroduction and warns against a sense of Finnish exceptionalism that could undermine trust in a rules-based world order, while Green MP Atte Harjanne argues that mines are a pragmatic way to protect Finland against a Russian attack.
The documentary explores the tension between military deterrence and humanitarian consequences, asking whether anti-personnel landmines can ever be used responsibly.
